## About this site

This site is the open, continuously updated companion to a peer-reviewed paper submitted to the **Journal of Open Hardware (JoOH)**. The journal article carries the peer-reviewed core: the research question, a condensed literature review, the framework, and headline recommendations. Everything that doesn't fit inside a 6,000-word journal article — full case studies, standalone position papers, the extended literature review, and audience-specific recommendations — lives here, and keeps growing after the paper is published.

> **Status:** structure only — content is being added section by section. See [Contributing](https://github.com/REPLACE-WITH-ORG/distributed-preparedness/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) if you're one of the co-authors adding material.

## Start here

- **[Framework](framework.qmd)** — the core argument: preparedness as distributed infrastructure rather than stockpiling.
- **[Literature Review](literature-review.qmd)** — the full review behind the paper's condensed version.
- **[Case Studies](case-studies/index.qmd)** — documented examples of makerspaces, distributed manufacturing, and offline connectivity in disaster response and preparedness.
- **[Position Papers](position-papers/index.qmd)** — standalone contributions from workshop participants.
- **[Recommendations](recommendations.qmd)** — actionable guidance for policymakers, humanitarian actors, makerspaces, and connectivity providers.
- **[About](about.qmd)** — authors, funder, license, and how to cite this project.
